factual_errors.text: Each collision pushes with a force. Billions of collisions per second make a pressure you can measure
factual_errors.correction: The number of collisions per second is vastly larger than billions. At room temperature and atmospheric pressure there are roughly 10^23 collisions per square centimetre of wall every second. Say 'huge numbers of collisions every second', as keyPoints[0].content already does.

factual_errors.text: It is simply billions of tiny molecules crashing into a container's walls, again and again.
factual_errors.correction: Even a small container of gas holds far more than billions of molecules. A litre of air at room conditions holds about 2.5 × 10^22 molecules. Say 'huge numbers of tiny molecules'.
